title: Apostrophes: plural, possessive, or both
subtitle: Form, Structure, and Sense · 19 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **19 of the official questions in Form, Structure, and Sense are this one** — 9 Easy, 8 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The four choices are the same word or words spelled with the apostrophe in different places: no apostrophe, 's, s, and s'.
- Often two nouns change at once, giving combinations like 'Xs Ys', 'X's Ys', and 'Xs' Y's'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For each noun, ask whether it owns the next noun.
- If it does, it needs an apostrophe.
- If it doesn't, it gets no apostrophe at all.
- 2) For each owner, use context to decide whether there is one owner or several.
- More than one ending in s takes s'.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices add an apostrophe to a noun that is only plural, such as a noun right before a verb or a plural object, or they pick the wrong owner count: 's when context names two or more owners, or s' when there is only one.
With two nouns, a choice can get one noun right and the other wrong.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
